C-KERNEL-STABLE-IPC-WASM-COMPONENT-BOUND.Title: Stable External Plugin Boundary v1: Native Process IPC, WASM Components, Capability Handles and Isolation

Constraints.Constraint: One logical capability contract is implemented by builtin, native-process and WASM Component providers; execution mode is not part of the consumer-visible contract and a consumer never needs execution-mode-specific code.

Public Rust ABI never crosses the external plugin boundary: no Rust struct layout as wire ABI, no trait object vtables, no raw pointers, no Arc/Rc, no panic unwinding; external adapters translate logical contracts into versioned WIT interfaces and versioned IPC envelopes.

External authority exists only through host-created, runtime-scoped, attenuated, revocable opaque handles; process isolation and sandboxing never replace capability broker authorization; plugin-supplied RuntimeId/PrincipalId/manifest data is never authoritative.
WASM components receive no ambient filesystem, network, clock, random or environment authority; explicit permissions are scoped and a manifest request never equals a granted permission.

Resource limits for memory, table entries, host-call concurrency and payload, invocation budget, wall-time and execution budget are part of the runtime admission and isolation contract; exhaustion maps to explicit failure classes without permanently consuming provider registry slots.

Trap, panic, child-process crash, protocol violation and resource exhaustion localize to one RuntimeId and never damage the host or unrelated runtimes; malformed external bytes never panic the kernel.
Stable repository-owned CI suite names remain unchanged and no essential M0.6 verification exists only in GitHub Actions YAML.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh local evidence covers three-mode conformance for one unchanged consumer, malicious WASM containment, native and WASM protocol robustness, opaque handle authority, external-provider restart continuity and stable repository CI suites; hosted CI remains unverified until a named GitHub Actions run exists.

C-KERNEL-STABLE-IPC-WASM-COMPONENT-BOUND.Summary:
Создать первый внешний plugin boundary Worldline, на котором один и тот же logical plugin/capability contract может быть реализован:
- builtin Rust provider; - trusted native out-of-process provider; - sandboxed WASM Component provider.
Consumer не должен знать, каким execution mode реализован provider.
Change должен доказать:
logical capability contract ↓ kernel/provider resolution ↓ execution adapter ├─ builtin Rust ├─ native process IPC └─ WASM Component ↓ same RpcOutcome / event / state / authority semantics
Public Rust trait/object ABI НЕ является внешним plugin ABI.
Native process и WASM boundaries используют versioned transport-neutral protocol contracts.
Authority через внешний boundary передаётся только через host-created opaque handles, scoped exact RuntimeId и attenuated до разрешённых operations / resources.
Plugin никогда не получает:
- raw Grant object; - SecurityStore; - StateBackend; - database/file handle; - arbitrary host PrincipalId authority; - unrestricted WASI environment.
WASM plugins получают только явно разрешённые host capabilities и минимальный WASI surface.
CPU, memory, wall-time и invocation resource limits являются частью runtime admission/isolation contract.
Trap, panic, child-process crash, protocol violation и resource exhaustion должны локализоваться в одном RuntimeId и не повреждать host или независимые runtimes.
Основной proving artifact change:
один reference provider реализован в builtin, native-process и WASM вариантах, а один unchanged consumer проходит один и тот же contract suite против всех трёх implementations.
Главный hostile test:
malicious WASM component пытается получить filesystem/network/state/ capability authority, которая ему не делегирована, подделать handles, превысить quotas и trap'нуться;
каждый такой путь должен либо получить deterministic denial, либо быть изолирован без повреждения остальных runtimes.

ArchitecturalInvariants.Invariant: EXECUTION MODE IS NOT PART OF THE LOGICAL CAPABILITY CONTRACT.
BUILTIN, NATIVE-PROCESS AND WASM PROVIDERS OBEY THE SAME AUTHORITY MODEL.
PUBLIC RUST ABI IS NOT THE WORLDLINE THIRD-PARTY ABI.
NO RUST TRAIT OBJECT, Arc<dyn Any>, STRUCT LAYOUT OR PANIC ABI CROSSES THE EXTERNAL PLUGIN BOUNDARY.
PROCESS ISOLATION DOES NOT CREATE AUTHORITY.
SANDBOXING DOES NOT REPLACE CAPABILITY AUTHORIZATION.
EXTERNAL PLUGIN AUTHORITY EXISTS ONLY THROUGH HOST-CREATED OPAQUE HANDLES.
A HANDLE IS VALID ONLY FOR THE RUNTIME AND LIFETIME THAT OWNS IT.
HANDLE VALUES ARE NOT GLOBALLY MEANINGFUL IDENTITIES.
GUESSING OR REPLAYING A HANDLE NEVER CREATES AUTHORITY.
STATE CONTINUES TO BELONG TO INSTALLATION, NOT PROCESS OR WASM INSTANCE.
CRASHED EXTERNAL RUNTIME LOSES LIVE HANDLES, GRANTS, STATE LEASES AND PROVIDER PUBLICATIONS.
UNTRUSTED CODE RECEIVES NO AMBIENT FILESYSTEM, NETWORK, CLOCK OR RANDOM AUTHORITY.
RESOURCE EXHAUSTION BY ONE PLUGIN MUST NOT EXHAUST THE HOST WITHOUT BOUNDS.
TRANSPORT FAILURE IS NOT CAPABILITY FAILURE SEMANTICS UNTIL THE BROKER CLASSIFIES IT.
IPC/WASM ADAPTERS DO NOT INVENT A SECOND RPC OR EVENT MODEL.

Goals.Goal: Зафиксировать external plugin ABI strategy ADR.
Ввести transport-neutral representation lifecycle и capability invocation.
Сохранить существующий builtin Rust path через тот же logical contract.
Дать external plugins state только через installation-bound host contract.
Ввести package manifest и compatibility metadata.
Доказать identical consumer semantics на трёх provider execution modes.

RequiredADR.Requirement: ADR explicitly rejects public Rust dylib ABI for third-party plugins.
ADR records exact supported Component Model/WASI baseline selected by implementation rather than saying "latest".

ExecutionModes.Mode:
Trusted Rust code linked into Worldline host.
Still uses ordinary RuntimeId, authority, lifecycle, state lease and capability contracts.
Third-party/untrusted component running through selected Component Model runtime with least-authority host imports.
ExecutionModes.Invariant: PluginDefinition semantics do not branch by product role.

ExternalAbiModel.Principle:
Logical Worldline contracts are ABI-neutral.
External adapters translate them into: - WIT interfaces/resources for WASM; - versioned IPC envelopes for native process.

Forbidden.Value: Rust struct memory layout as wire ABI
serde representation without explicit protocol version contract

ExternalAbiModel.Requirement: Unknown fields/versions are handled according to explicit compatibility rules, never accidental parser behaviour.
Boundary payload size is bounded before allocation.

PluginPackageIdentity.Rule: PackageVersion is independent from capability contract versions.
Package identity does not itself grant authority.

PluginManifest.Invariant: Manifest describes requested/declared permissions. It does not grant them.
PluginManifest.Requirement: Unknown mandatory manifest fields/schema versions fail closed.
Paths inside package cannot escape package root.

WitBoundary.Purpose: Define first external component contracts without exposing kernel Rust API.
WitBoundary.Requirement: Exact WIT package/module names may differ after implementation review, but responsibilities remain separated.
WitBoundary.Rule: WIT lifecycle does not expose arbitrary Kernel object.
Capability invocation does not provide direct provider registry access.
Event publication remains separate from capability invocation.
State access uses installation-scoped host resource/handle.

NativeIpcProtocol.Requirement: Host assigns authoritative runtime/security identity after successful handshake/admission.
Every request/response is correlated by explicit bounded protocol identity.
In-flight request count and queued bytes are bounded.
Unknown or malformed message does not crash host.
Protocol violation may terminate/quarantine offending RuntimeId.

OpaqueAuthorityHandles.Purpose: External plugin can refer to delegated authority without receiving kernel Grant/Principal internals.

HandleProperties.Property: non-persistent unless explicitly represented by another contract

OpaqueAuthorityHandles.Invariant: Handle value alone is not globally reusable authority.
Handle lookup always includes exact RuntimeId/session ownership.
Old handle from crashed/restarted RuntimeId is invalid.
Numeric/string guessing cannot access another runtime's handle table.
OpaqueAuthorityHandles.Rule: Guest cannot widen scope encoded by host handle metadata.
Delegation can only produce equal-or-narrower authority.

ExternalStateAccess.Invariant: WASM/native plugin never receives StateBackend/database/file object.
ExternalStateAccess.Requirement: State operations are routed through existing installation-owned state contract.
Host binds state handle to exact InstallationId and RuntimeStateLease.
Runtime termination invalidates all live external state handles and open transaction handles.
Restart creates new runtime state handles while preserving installation state.

WasiAuthority.Principle: WASI capability availability is explicit least-authority host policy.
WasiAuthority.Filesystem:
No ambient host filesystem access.
Preopened directory/resource, if permitted, is explicitly scoped.
WasiAuthority.Network:
No ambient outbound/inbound network access.
Network permission is explicitly enabled/scoped.
WasiAuthority.Clock: Clock access may be omitted or restricted where unnecessary.
WasiAuthority.Random: Random source is explicitly provided if requested/approved.
WasiAuthority.Environment: Host environment variables are not inherited by default.

RequiredDimensions.Limit: CPU/fuel/epoch or selected runtime-equivalent execution budget

ResourceLimits.Rule: Exact enforcement mechanism is runtime-specific but observable semantics are shared.
Limit exhaustion maps to explicit runtime/invocation failure class.
Resource exhaustion does not permanently consume provider registry slot.

FailureMapping.Requirement: Each physical failure maps into existing runtime/RPC failure semantics without pretending all failures are PluginError.
Failure classification remains observable for diagnostics.
Runtime terminal cleanup revokes handles, state leases, grants, subscriptions and provider publications.

ProcessSupervision.Requirement: Native provider child process is owned by one RuntimeId.
Unexpected process exit transitions only that runtime through existing crash/restart/quarantine policy.
Child stdout/stderr is bounded/handled such that plugin cannot deadlock host by filling inherited pipe.
After deadline host may terminate owned child process.
Killing native child process must not kill host.

ReferenceExternalPlugin.Purpose: Prove transport equivalence without browser/agent/UI-specific semantics.
ReferenceExternalPlugin.Invariant: Consumer implementation and logical CapabilityId do not change when provider execution mode changes.
ReferenceExternalPlugin.Requirement: All implementations pass the same semantic contract suite.
Stateful operation uses same InstallationId persistence semantics.
Observation uses same M0.4 event transport semantics.

MaliciousWasmSuite.Attempt: Read host file without filesystem permission.
Open network connection without network permission.
Widen resource scope encoded in handle.
Commit old transaction after runtime termination.
Flood host calls beyond concurrency/queue limits.
MaliciousWasmSuite.Invariant: Every attempt produces denial/contained failure and leaves unrelated reference runtime usable.

ImplementationGuidance.Guidance: Do not begin by embedding a WASM runtime everywhere in worldline-kernel.
First define transport-neutral external runtime/host-call interfaces.
Keep execution adapters in dedicated crates/modules where possible.

Recommended decomposition:
worldline-kernel logical runtime/security/contracts
worldline-plugin-protocol ABI-neutral protocol/manifest vocabulary
worldline-native-host child process supervision + IPC adapter
worldline-wasm-host Component runtime + host imports
worldline-reference-external cross-mode reference plugin/tests
Exact crate names may differ, but database/WASM/process implementation dependencies should not spread through kernel.
Do not optimize IPC with shared memory in v1.
Do not attempt zero-copy before semantics are stable.
Do not expose all WASI and then try to deny sensitive operations inside plugin code.
Start from no ambient WASI capability and explicitly add only what tests require.
Never serialize Grant or Principal authority object into guest payload.
If native process is considered trusted, still route its capability calls through broker.
Prefer one small external reference plugin over prematurely porting browser or agent code into WASM.

SuggestedExecutionOrder.Step: Inventory current runtime/RPC/event/state interfaces that external adapter must preserve.
Write ADR and pin Component/WASI + native IPC choices.
Introduce package manifest and protocol identities.
Extract transport-neutral external provider adapter contract.
Implement runtime-scoped opaque host handle table.
Implement native child supervision and lifecycle adapter.
Add malicious WASM and malformed IPC suites.
Add external-provider S1 persistence/restart proving paths.
Integrate into stable repository CI suites.
Update GRACE projection/ADR/ROADMAP only after evidence passes.

Пересекает ли boundary хоть один Rust-specific ABI type?
Может ли external plugin выбрать себе RuntimeId/PrincipalId?
Можно ли скопировать opaque handle в другой runtime и использовать?
Можно ли использовать handle после restart?
Может ли manifest самостоятельно дать plugin requested permission?

FailureConditions.Failure: Public plugin ABI зависит от Rust struct/vtable layout.
WASM sandbox считается достаточной заменой authorization.
Handle можно использовать из другого RuntimeId.
Handle переживает runtime restart как authority.
Один malicious guest может crash/DoS unrelated runtime без configured bound.
Protocol/WIT adapter создаёт вторую несовместимую RPC/event semantics.
Product-specific browser/agent/UI types входят в external ABI.

ExitCriteria.Criterion: Worldline has a documented versioned external plugin ABI boundary.
Public external plugin ABI does not rely on Rust binary ABI.
Builtin, native-process and WASM providers satisfy one logical contract.
Unchanged consumer works across all three execution modes.
External authority crosses boundaries only via opaque runtime-scoped attenuated handles.
WASM environment is least-authority and resource-bounded.
Native provider is supervised and restartable independently of host.
Trap, crash, malformed input and resource exhaustion are contained.
Installation state survives provider process/component restart while live authority does not.
Malicious WASM plugin cannot read/invoke/store anything outside explicit delegation.
M0.6 behavior is proven through stable CI and end-to-end proving paths.
Kernel is ready for compatibility/update/operability work without another external ABI identity redesign.
